key_insight: Generating plausible protein–ligand binding poses is not enough—choosing the best one remains difficult. Pyrite benchmarks this challenge with 1,500 pose pairs, on which expert chemists using 3D visualization and physics-based scores perform near chance.
problem_solved: The paper addresses how to evaluate systems that rank candidate protein–ligand binding poses, a key bottleneck in turning cofolding predictions into useful drug-discovery insights.
method: Introduce Pyrite, a pairwise pose-ranking benchmark containing 1,500 pose pairs across diverse protein–ligand complexes.
Evaluate expert chemists equipped with 3D visualization tools and physics-based scores.
Use pairwise ranking to assess the difficulty of selecting between candidate binding poses.
impact: Pyrite gives AI/ML practitioners a benchmark for evaluating pose-ranking systems beyond pose generation. Near-chance expert performance highlights the need for more reliable ranking methods.
visual_elements: Side-by-side 3D views of two candidate ligand poses inside the same protein pocket.
Workflow diagram: candidate poses → pairwise comparison → ranking decision.
Qualitative performance chart showing expert ranking near the chance baseline, without inventing exact scores.
Benchmark badge highlighting 1,500 pose pairs across diverse complexes.
paper_title: Pyrite: Building and Benchmarking Protein-Ligand Pose Ranking Agents
paper_authors: Megha Srivastava, Michael H. Lim, Allison M. Keys, Pranav Murugan, Nate Gruver
